tagline: River to river, the long way round to Portland.
intro: From Westfir the Aufderheide Drive joins the North Fork of the Middle Fork Willamette and runs up its canyon between rock walls a thousand feet high. It comes down the South Fork McKenzie past Cougar Reservoir to the Delta trail, where Douglas firs and western red cedars stand up to 500 years old.

Then the byway works north along the McKenzie, over to the North Santiam and down to Detroit Lake, and up the Breitenbush River on Forest Road 46. At Ripplebrook it meets the Clackamas and follows it to Estacada, a town that grew up on hydropower and logging. There are faster ways from Eugene to Portland.
season: Late spring through fall, by the state's trip notes.

moments.title: Office Bridge
moments.text: Oregon's longest covered bridge, 180 feet of triple Howe truss built in 1944 to carry log trucks to the Westfir mill, with a separate walkway for people on foot.

moments.title: Breitenbush
moments.text: A hot springs community named for Lewis Breitenbucher, a one-armed hunter who credited his night vision to a bat's eye under his tongue. The legislator who mapped it got the name wrong.

moments.title: Three Lynx
moments.text: A power company town twenty miles east of Estacada, begun as Camp 8 in 1923 and lived in until 2020, when its last few houses came down.

practical: Forest Roads 19 and 46 are generally closed by snow from November 15 to April 30.
